analysis.investment_thesis: Emcure passes on business quality (ROCE 20.7%) but fails the Magic Formula's affordability test — Earnings Yield of ~4.5% (EBIT INR 1,469 Cr / EV ~INR 32,600 Cr) is well below the 6% minimum, meaning the market is paying a steep premium for this quality. Without cheapness, there is no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Return on Capital just clears the bar: ROCE 20.7% and ROE 18.5% show decent capital efficiency
Debt significantly reduced: Total Debt fell from INR 2,335 Cr (2024) to INR 1,023 Cr (2025), D/E now 0.34
Consistent OCF generation: 5/5 years positive; INR 852 Cr OCF in FY25 on INR 707 Cr net profit
key_risks: Expensive by Magic Formula standards: P/E 35x, EV/EBITDA 19.84x — Earnings Yield just 4.5%, far below 6% floor
Anaemic revenue growth: 9% CAGR over 6 years — barely outpaces inflation and inadequate for the valuation premium
FCF volatility: capex of INR 397–407 Cr annually consumes 40–80% of OCF, making FCF erratic (INR 345 Cr in 2023 vs INR 801 Cr in 2024)
red_flags: Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) ≈ 4.5% — fails the Magic Formula minimum of 6%; stock is overvalued on this metric
Operating margin only 15% on 59% gross margin implies heavy SG&A/R&D spend, limiting earnings power leverage
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Emcure: EBIT (Operating Income) for FY25 is INR 1,469 Cr. Enterprise Value = Market Cap INR 31,701 Cr + Net Debt ~INR 901 Cr = ~INR 32,600 Cr. Earnings Yield = 4.5% — well below the 6% floor I require before even considering a name. ROCE at 20.7% clears the 20% threshold but barely, and is not the 25%+ I'd want for a business commanding a 35x P/E. Neither metric is strong enough to clear the Magic Formula bar simultaneously.

The business itself is decent — diverse pharma therapeutic mix, promoter-heavy ownership (77.9%), declining interest burden, and the Novo Nordisk GLP-1 partnership adds optionality. But "decent" at 35x P/E is not a bargain. Revenue has grown at only 9% CAGR over six years, EBITDA CAGR is just 6.3%, and net profit growth has been lumpy (INR 562 Cr in 2023, INR 528 Cr in 2024, INR 707 Cr in 2025). The magic formula demands both cheapness AND quality — Emcure offers partial quality at a full price. I'd revisit if the stock corrects to an Earnings Yield above 8% (implying ~INR 1,000/share).
